title: Repair cURL parsing and unsupported-option reporting
description:
Replace positional token guessing with a small shell-aware tokenizer and an option parser. The leading `curl` executable must never be treated as the URL. Correctly handle single/double quotes, escapes, whitespace, and line continuations without executing shell syntax. Support the approved subset: `-X/--request`, `-H/--header`, `-d/--data` variants, `-F/--form`, `-k/--insecure`, `-L/--location`, `--url`, `-u/--user`, and `-b/--cookie`.

Define repeated data-option semantics and the precedence between explicit method, data-implied POST, and URL arguments. Never auto-read `@file` values; preserve them as unresolved input and warn that local file loading is unsupported. Unknown, ambiguous, or potentially dangerous options must generate structured warnings tied to the original token instead of being silently discarded.

The import UI must preview the parsed request and warnings before saving. A comprehensive fixture suite should cover common browser/Postman cURL output, quoting edge cases, repeated flags, malformed commands, unsupported options, and round-trip normalization.

checklist.text: Implement a non-executing tokenizer for quotes, escapes, whitespace, and line continuations
Parse the supported short and long options without treating the curl executable as a URL
Define URL, method, repeated data, header, cookie, auth, redirect, TLS, and multipart precedence
Treat @file input as unresolved text and never access local files implicitly
Return token-specific structured warnings for unsupported, ambiguous, missing-value, and dangerous options
Add an import preview that shows the normalized request and requires acknowledgement of warnings
Test browser/Postman fixtures, quotes, continuations, repeated flags, malformed input, warnings, and normalization
